prompt: A photorealistic medium shot, 16:9, of a masked presenter on a 1989 American public-access cable show, captured on a tripod camcorder: slightly soft, reds bleeding a little, the white areas clipping. He stands beside a folding table against a brown carpet backdrop, jabbing a gloved finger at a hand-drawn chart on an easel whose marker line plunges off the bottom of the board, his other hand raised palm-up in a shrug. A charcoal-grey rib-knit balaclava covers his whole head, the face one continuous unbroken knitted surface, the crown shaped with decreases, light pilling on the cheeks. A large cream-white felt ring is stitched around the face, and one small solid red felt triangle with rounded corners sits high inside the ring on the right side of the picture, at two o'clock. Crumpled black suit jacket, white shirt buttoned to the throat over the hood's neck, plain black leather gloves creased at the knuckles, cuffs past the wrists. A single overhead fluorescent tube lights him from above. Off-centre framing, head large in frame. Thanks.

A photorealistic medium shot, 16:9, of a masked comic presenter on a deliberately cheap homemade set built from flattened cardboard boxes and silver gaffer tape, photographed on a 35mm compact camera with a 28mm lens. Behind him a cardboard bank facade with painted columns sags forward; he braces it with one gloved palm and tears a strip of gaffer tape off the roll with the other hand, mid-repair, shoulders hunched. A black merino balaclava covers his whole head, the face one smooth continuous knitted surface with a soft fuzzy nap and a loose thread at the temple. A large cream-white felt ring is appliquéd around the face with a visible edge stitch, and one small solid red felt triangle with rounded corners sits high inside it, on the right side of the frame at two o'clock. Black roll-neck folded over the hood's neck, crumpled black suit jacket, black leather gloves each carrying a thumbnail-sized stitched patch of the same white ring and red triangle on the back. One bare clamp work lamp from frame left throws a hard shadow across the cardboard. Head large and off-centre. Thanks.
